findings.title: Public schema misses mixed percent-encoded prefixed and encoded-equals assignments
findings.observation: The public event schema accepted mixed percent-encoded client-secret assignments in free-form metadata, labels, and terminal reasons. The accepted forms included a percent-encoded prefix separator with percent-encoded letters and assignments whose equals separator was percent-encoded. Runtime and store paths rejected the same values, so the schema-only boundary is inconsistent with the authoritative detector.
findings.proof: independent-probes.json findings named assignment-percent-prefixed-mixed, assignment-percent-equals, and assignment-percent-prefixed-equals

findings.title: One-pass decoding permits double-encoded assignments and JSON credential keys
findings.observation: Double-encoded assignment and JSON-key forms survived the runtime detector, crossed normalizeMetadata, normalizeConnectionDefinition, normalizeConnectionEvent, and normalizeReason, and reached createConnectionStore. The store appended one event for each double-encoded form. A single decodeURIComponent pass leaves the second escape layer for the literal regex/JSON checks.
findings.proof: independent-probes.json findings named percent-json-key-encoded-brace and percent-double-assignment; both store cases report appended: 1

findings.title: Public schema does not mirror percent-encoded URL credential shapes
findings.observation: A percent-encoded URL scheme and delimiters were accepted by public metadata, label, and terminal-reason validation while runtime and store detection rejected the decoded URL form. The public URL pattern only recognizes literal URL schemes and the percent-encoded shape helper contains no URL alternative.

findings.title: Public schema does not mirror percent-encoded provider-token prefixes
findings.observation: A provider-token prefix with percent-encoded letters and separator was accepted by public metadata, label, and terminal-reason validation while runtime and store detection rejected the decoded provider-token form. The public provider-token pattern and percent-encoded helper do not cover this representation.
